notes.title: Wild Assault Dev Log #38: An Open Letter to All from 《Wild Assault》
notes.content: [h3]Dear Wild Ones,[/h3][p][/p][p]We hope this letter finds you well.[/p][p][/p][p]First and foremost, we would like to extend our sincerest gratitude to every player who has stood by [i]Wild Assault[/i]. Your feedback, every battle you’ve fought, and every suggestion you’ve shared on our forums and community platforms have been the driving force behind our continuous efforts to improve the game.[/p][p][/p][p]Recently, our team’s focus has shifted to a new phase of development. We’ve dedicated most of our resources to enhancing [b]Custom Rooms[/b], designing [b]new maps[/b], and optimizing [b]core gameplay experiences[/b]. However, due to limited development capacity, some of the originally planned content—such as large-scale events—will be adjusted in scale. The specific changes are as follows:[/p][p][/p][p]1、The [b]content volume of the Battle Pass will be significantly reduced[/b]. We will also [b]lower its price[/b] and transition it into a [b]self-sustaining model[/b].[/p][p]2、The development progress of the [b]Snow Leopard hero has fallen behind schedule[/b] due to higher-than-expected complexity. We will need [b]more time to refine this hero[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]That said, we’re excited to confirm that the [b]Snowfield Map will be released as scheduled[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]Moving forward, we will continue to adopt an [b]iterative and agile approach[/b] to updates, ensuring all plans are communicated transparently through official announcements.[/p][p][/p][p]To our dedicated players: the story of [i]Wild Assault [/i]is far from over. Our inbox and community channels remain open to you—every suggestion you offer could become a critical reference for our next phase of adjustments.[/p][p]We sail together through storms, and the future remains bright.[/p][p][/p][p]Sincerely,[/p][p]The Combat Cat Studio[/p][p]September 19, 2025[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]X：[url="https://x.com/WildAssaultGame"]https://x.com/WildAssaultGame[/url][/p][p]Discord：[url="https://discord.gg/WildAssault"]https://discord.gg/WildAssault[/url][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Follow us on social media ⤵️[/h3]

notes.title: Wild Assault September 4 Hotfix Patch Notes-BOT Optimization Phase One
notes.content: [p][b]Hello Wild Ones,[/b][/p][p]We will be performing [b]a live update at 3:00 AM PT on September 4. [/b]Ongoing matches will not be affected during the update, but matchmaking will be temporarily unavailable. Please exit the game, update your game client via Steam, and then relaunch the game.[/p][p][/p][p]We've noticed community feedback expressing dissatisfaction with our BOT mechanics and performance, along with many valuable suggestions. As a result, we've reprioritized our development focus to address these concerns as our top priority. This update marks the first phase of our BOT optimizations.[/p][p]Simultaneously, we're adjusting our update strategy and development rhythm as follows:[/p][p]• [b]Reprioritization[/b]: The team will dedicate full efforts to optimizing core experiences (BOT logic improvements, core gameplay, controller support, etc.).[/p][p]• [b]Flexible Update Strategy[/b]: Due to our limited team size, we'll adopt a "small, rapid iterations" approach: features will be released immediately upon completion rather than waiting for large bundled updates.[/p][p]• [b]Continuous Content Iteration[/b]: Future content—such as custom rooms, new maps, and new heroes in development—will follow the "complete first, update first" strategy.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]▌ [/b]BOT [b]Optimizations Phase One[/b][/h3][p]• Fixed BOT using skills while simultaneously firing.[/p][p]• Fixed BOT performing instant 180-degree turns and aim at very close range.[/p][p]• Fixed BOT firing immediately after tactical sprints.[/p][p]• Fixed abnormal fire rates for specific weapons used by BOT.[/p][p]• Optimized BOT jumping logic to resolve unnatural jumping behaviors.[/p][p]• Improved BOT decision-making logic to address instances of ignoring smoke effects.[/p][h3][b]▌ Sextans Reward Adjustment[/b]:[/h3][p]• After the new season of the Sextans launched, we received feedback about players unable to obtain S2 limited rewards in time. Post-update, S2 limited rewards will be added to the current Sextans! (Wild ones who already reached the corresponding tiers need not worry—we’ll compensate via in-game mail within 1 week.)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/53374795c46718d64cd6ac2d74d37fb29d6f8e60.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]▌ VALIANT WEEKEND[/b][/h3][p]• During the event, participating in matches grants [b]150% Valiant Proficiency[/b].[/p][h3][b]▌ Fixes[/b][/h3][p]• Fixed inability to interact with ammo supply crates when the interaction key was set to H.[/p][p]• Fixed incorrect weapon attachment descriptions displaying after resolution changes.[/p][p]• Fixed abnormal visual effects for Jack’s "Costa Groove" skin on Medium graphics settings.[/p][p]• Fixed incorrect "outside safe zone" prompts when defenders were revived in combat areas during retreat phases.[/p][p]• Fixed inability to deploy using the spacebar in TRAINING.[/p][p][/p][p]Combat Cat Studio[/p][p][/p][h3]Follow us on social media ⤵️[/h3]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/4da53fa263833a6113ce7554222ad3ebd62cfdaf.png[/img]

Hello Wild Ones!

[b]#TGIF![/b] 🎉 Wishing you a joyful weekend ahead! In this episode, we will be talking about our recent development adjustments, while letting you know more about our upcoming new Valiant - Crock! Without further ado, let's get right into it!

[h1]1. Improving the Core Gameplay 🎛️[/h1]

Based on the feedback we've collected up to this point, we've noticed that many of our players have shared suggestions regarding Wild Assault's core combat smoothness. After extensive discussions, the studio decided to [b]shift some of our focus from new content development to core gameplay optimization.[/b] After all, what initially drew everyone to Wild Assault was the satisfying combat experience it offers. Therefore, we will prioritize addressing the current pain points in our gameplay mechanics. Now we'd like to briefly introduce the dedicated plan we've come up with for gameplay fluidity improvement.

[h1]2. Gameplay Fluidity R&D Brief 📋[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Custom modes will be postponed to allow us more time for fine-tuning and polishing.
[*] Another round of comprehensive balance review and adjustment is on the way. We'll also keep you updated on our progress throughout the R&D process.
[*] Gameplay Fluidity Enhancement Plan
[olist]
[*] The gameplay fluidity enhancement plan will focus on core combat modules, covering 4 key areas:
[olist]
[*] Basic 3C optimization (Character, Camera, Controls)
[*] Gunfight combat experience optimization
[*] Valiant ability experience optimization
[*] Game map interaction optimization
[/olist]
[*] Our optimization strategy operates on two dimensions:
[olist]
[*] The responsiveness between input and visual feedback.
[*] The match between input delay and combat rhythm. This means we'll evaluate whether the startup and recovery frames of various actions fit their intended use cases and meet design expectations, adjusting operations that have excessively long startup or recovery times.
[/olist]
[*] Specific optimizations will include many elements such as run-and-gun mechanics, hip fire and ADS transitions, reloading and weapon switching, tactical sprint, ability operations, and more. Most of the content in this plan is expected to meet you all in Season 2.
[/olist] [/olist]
[h1]3. New Valiant: Crock! 🐊[/h1]

Based on our previous reveal of the 11th Valiant Crock, many of you have already guessed what animal he is. [b]Yes! Crock is our new cold-blooded crocodile warrior, the first reptile ever to join the Wild Assault Valiant lineup![/b] Now we'd like to share Crock's fanart reference and lore with you:

[quote][i]"It's time. Now we play for keeps." - Crock[/i]

Whether in the past or present, Crock has always been the ultimate hunter. The only difference now is that his prey has shifted from politicians to soldiers.

His exceptional combat skills and lightning-fast adaptability make him unstoppable on every mission. Even the most secure defense systems crumble before him like paper. His talents quickly earned him a reputation as the organization's most sought-after assassin, with high-priority and challenging contracts flooding in one after another.

However, he gradually lost interest through countless "mind-numbingly boring" assignments, until he insisted on quitting and found himself on the organization's hit list. The experience of fighting other trained killers in life-or-death battles reignited his desire for combat. Compared to defenseless politicians, skilled opponents offered far more excitement and challenge.

After effortlessly escaping the assassin organization's pursuit, he received an offer from the Desolate Legion. This time, he accepted with genuine enthusiasm...... [/quote]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/4da53fa263833a6113ce7554222ad3ebd62cfdaf.png[/img]

Hello Wild Ones!

As promised, here comes the new dev log for this week. We'll be addressing the major community concerns about the new content this week, along with the latest updates on optimizations and bug fixes.

[h1]About the Akai Hime - Haru Silk Series[/h1]

As part of the Kit Carnival event, we released the Haru Silk Series cosmetics, which sparked major discussions among the community. [b]First, we'd like to extend a huge thanks to the Wild Ones who've already supported us by making a purchase. We hope you're enjoying the series! [/b]

Since its release, we've been carefully monitoring community discussions and feedback. [b]We recognize that the pricing for this series didn't meet our community's expectations, and we understand the various concerns this has raised. [/b]

During this early access phase, our team is exploring appropriate monetization strategies. This process is necessary, but we admit our current approach has not been fully refined. [b]We are genuinely sorry for any inconveniences this might have caused. Our sincere apologies![/b]

[b]We earnestly invite you to collaborate with us in finding a balanced model that both sustains Wild Assault's development and ensures players can experience and enjoy the content we've poured our hearts into.[/b] Our studio's commitment remains unchanged: [b]transparent communication and continuous improvement based on the community's preferences![/b]

Therefore, after carefully evaluating your feedback and our development plan, we are announcing the following adjustments:
[olist]
[*] [b]Lower the pricing for related items and bundles, and apply this reduced pricing to subsequent content of the same level quality.[/b]
[*] Revised pricing for the Haru Silk series items will be effective after the update at [b]3 AM PT on May 23:[/b]
[olist]
[*] [b]Haru Silk Bundle:[/b] Reduced permanently from 3,080 to 2,180 Beast Coins [b](30% reduced)[/b]. 
[*] [b]Akai Hime - Haru Silk:[/b] Reduced permanently from 1,840 to 1,150 Beast Coins [b](37% reduced)[/b].
[*] [b]VS_VAL - Haru Silk:[/b] Reduced permanently from 1,300 to 800 Beast Coins [b](38% reduced)[/b].
[*] [b]Haru Silk Squad Animation:[/b] Reduced permanently from 620 to 500 Beast Coins [b](19% reduced)[/b].
[*] [b]Haru Silk Avatar and Valiant Card:[/b] Reduced permanently from 310 to 200 Beast Coins [b](35% reduced)[/b].
[/olist]
[*] For Wild Ones who purchased the above items before this price adjustment, [b]we will issue Beast Coins refunds before 3 AM PT, May 29.[/b]
[*] Akai Hime - Haru Silk leg hair adjustment: Your feedback has been heard! We will continue to monitor community input and implement improvements accordingly.
[/olist]
[h1]About Limited-Time Deathmatch Mode[/h1]

[h2]Addressing Concerns About Splitting Playerbase[/h2]

WA Conquest and WA Raid are Wild Assault's primary modes. We will continue to focus on and refine large-scale battleground game modes, continuously optimizing the player experience and introducing new content.

The two new Deathmatch modes we're introducing are designed as alternative modes to enrich players' overall game experience. We will periodically release similar modes and event-based modes. However, our core gameplay modes will maintain their primary status.

[h2]About Limited Availability[/h2]

The reason for limited availability of the new game modes is to provide the best possible gameplay experience for everyone. Since these modes require a certain player base, we've chosen the two time slots with the highest concurrent player counts.

This approach is also intended to prevent player fragmentation that could compromise the gameplay quality. We have received your feedback regarding the limited availability, and we appreciate it! [b]We will continuously adjust the availability based on player engagement with these two new modes, and we welcome your further suggestions! [/b]

[h1]Regarding Map Balance[/h1]

Following our previous weekly update discussing the Valiant and weapon balance, our next critical task is optimizing the [b]balance of game modes and maps.[/b] We've noticed that players frequently discuss balance issues between attacking and defending sides in the WA Raid mode.

We plan to collect community feedback through a survey in the near future, and ultimately combine this input with backend data to assess potential balance adjustment strategies. At present, [b]we'll address the specific concerns raised about The Crescent Bay.[/b]

Through active player feedback and backend data monitoring, [b]we've discovered that the first area of The Crescent Bay in WA Raid is critically unbalancing gameplay. The win rates for attacking and defending sides in this area have reached an alarming 3:7 ratio.[/b] We have already identified the primary issue: [b]an unreasonable cover structure on a key pathway that has caused significant player data clustering.[/b]

[b]Simultaneously, we will further optimize the structure design of the first area, addressing the defensive line-of-sight advantage that players have highlighted.[/b] Our goal is to provide both sides with a more comfortable and engaging combat experience. We are currently conducting internal testing for these structural modifications and will soon deliver the updated design for community review.

[b]Similarly, we are optimizing the final combat area.[/b] Although it has met our initial design expectations for creating intense confrontations between both sides, it's clear that in this "final sprint," the two sides are not starting on equal footing. Even after brutal game points elimination, the attacking side finds it extremely difficult to break through the seemingly impenetrable defensive line. We will slightly reduce the defending side's advantages while preserving the current gameplay experience, aiming to deliver a more intense and thrilling attack-defense dynamic.

[h1]Weekly Update Changelog May 23[/h1]

[h2]Optimizations[/h2]
[olist]
[*] Haru Silk series pricing adjustment.
[*] Higher drop rate for Kite Dye.
[/olist]

[*] [b]New Map for Season 2:[/b] Overall structure has been completed. We're now refining details for objects and obstacles.

Feel free to let us know what you think in the comments! Thank you all again and hope you enjoy a lovely weekend! 🫶🫡

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/4da53fa263833a6113ce7554222ad3ebd62cfdaf.png[/img]

Hello Wild Ones!

[b]#TGIF! 🎉[/b]

In last week's dev log, we discussed our approach to balancing weapons and Valiants. Since then, we've been closely following your discussions in the comments and on social media. These conversations helped us recognize where our perspectives differ from yours, as well as your desire for more transparency about our current work.

This week's dev log will continue addressing your feedback while sharing updates on our progress. 🫡

[h1]1. Weapon Balancing[/h1]

In the previous dev log, the adjustment approach for the NK-47 sparked particularly active discussions. We received a lot of player feedback pointing out that [b]other ARs feel underpowered compared to the NK-47. Additionally, there was significant feedback regarding the PKP.[/b]

As we've mentioned before, weapon balancing is an ongoing process that considers both objective data and player experience feedback. [b]Currently, we're still conducting comprehensive analysis and evaluation for each weapon. Once we've identified the key issues, we'll implement corresponding balance adjustments.[/b]

[h1]2. About Vladimir[/h1]

In the previous balance update, we slightly reduced the explosive damage of Vladimir’s tactical ability (Q) to address the excessive damage output from manually detonating it with gunfire. However, based on player feedback and collected data from the current version, Vladimir’s performance remains far ahead of other characters.

Moving forward, we’ll conduct further comprehensive adjustments to Vladimir’s balance. Our goal is to [b]maintain the intended effectiveness of his abilities while reducing his margin for error and tuning down some overperforming values.[/b]

[h1]3. New Content[/h1]

[h2]3.1 New Valiant[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Crock: [/b]The visual assets for the 11th Valiant, Crock, are now fully completed, and we're currently in the ability development phase. Can you guess what animal Crock actually is and what his Class will be? Feel free to share your theories and discuss with us in the comments!
[*] [b]New Valiant Poll: [/b]Thanks to everyone who voted in last week’s character design poll! [b]We received 4,354 responses, and the snow leopard emerged as the clear winner with 41.27% of the votes, way ahead of the rest![/b] Now that the poll is closed, the snow leopard design will move into the art development phase. We’d love to hear your ideas for classes and abilities! Drop your suggestions in the comments to help inspire the final look!
[/list]
[h2]3.2 New Weapons[/h2]

Season 2's new weapon designs are now complete! We're currently fine-tuning their stats and balance. Stay tuned for more updates soon! In the meantime, what weapons would you like to see in Wild Assault next? Let us know in the comments!

[h2]3.3 Achievement[/h2]

Achievement System Sneak Peek!

The team’s brewing some spicy achievements. Here’s a peek at the wildest contenders. Can you guess how to unlock these? 👀
(Names are still works in progress!)
[list]
[*] Hyper Inhalation - "99.1% pure, no doubt!"
[*] Tiny but Deadly - "Size means nothing when skill strikes true!"
[*] Cornered Beast - "Wounded beast bites back harder."
[*] Just Vibing - "Enjoyed the cool animation. Totally worth it!"
[*] Fist of Furry - "🎶 Furry Fighting! Light Speed Striking! 🎶"
[/list]
[h1]4. Known Issues We're Working On[/h1]
[list]
[*] After disconnecting and reconnecting, the Valiant remains knocked down on the ground and cannot respawn.

notes.title: Wild Assault Dev Log #23: Balance, Matchmaking & Netcode Updates
notes.content:
[h1]1. The Dev Log is Back![/h1]

As promised, starting this Friday, we’ll continue sharing updates and staying connected with you through the Wild Assault Dev Log!

Combat Cat Studio is committed to Wild Assault's long-term development, with ongoing content updates and gameplay optimizations. During this challenging process, we truly need honest feedback from our Wild Ones. Staying closely connected with you all is exactly why we’re bringing back the Dev Log.

Following the discussions around our first balance patch on April 28, this week's Dev Log will give you [b]a behind-the-scenes look at our weapon and Valiant balance adjustments.[/b] We'll also address your questions about [b]matchmaking, network issues and share updates on our current development progress.[/b]

[h1]2. Weapon Balacing Logic[/h1]

It’s important to understand that balancing is a massive and complex task. Adjustments involve numerous factors, including Valiant base stats, movement capabilities, abilities, talents, weapons available to each class, and attachment settings.

To minimize negative impacts on gameplay, we approach balance changes with extreme caution. Before implementing our first major balance update, we gathered player feedback through surveys. The final adjustments were determined by analyzing both player responses and backend data.

Below is an overview of our approach to the first weapon balance update:
[b](1m ≈ 3.28 ft)[/b]

[h2]2.1 NK Assault Rifle: Adjusting Mid-to-Long Range Dominance for Tactical Balance[/h2]

In previous versions, the NK rifle dominated mid-to-long-range engagements due to its minimal bullet spread and highly stable recoil. [b]Backend data showed that the NK had an overwhelming lead in kill efficiency and pick rate beyond 50 meters, which led to stale tactical choices, while other rifles like the M4 and AUG saw lower usage.[/b]

We believe the NK’s core strengths should lie in close-to-mid-range burst damage and handling feedback. To reinforce this, we’ve increased its overall bullet spread, making sustained fire less accurate. This change isn’t a direct nerf to the NK’s power but rather encourages players to control their firing patterns more precisely:
[list]
[*] Burst fire remains stable for controlled shots.
[*] Full-auto spraying now requires stronger recoil control to compensate for the wider spread.
[/list]
[b]Testing data shows the NK’s hit rate beyond 50 meters dropped by 13%, while its close-to-mid-range (30–50m) kill efficiency remained consistent.[/b] The goal is to incentivize sniper/DMR use for long-range fights, and preserving the NK’s mid-range viability as a tactical option.

[h2]2.2 Shotguns: Limiting One-Shot Kill Range, Enhancing Tactical Depth[/h2]

Shotgun adjustments were a key focus in this balance update. [b]Data showed that shotguns had an 85%+ one-shot kill rate within 15 meters, with an average engagement distance of just 7.2 meters.[/b] This "point-blank dominance" led to players over relying on shotguns in close-quarters combat, severely limiting the viability of other weapons.

To restore diversity in close-range engagements, we [b]reduced the effective range[/b] of shotguns and [b]slightly decreased pellet density.[/b] This means players must now more [b]carefully control engagement distances,[/b] while opponents gain a better chance to counterattack. For example, if a shotgun user fails to land critical hits at close range, enemies now have a higher chance to fight back with SMGs or pistols.

We intentionally [b]preserved the shotgun’s one-shot kill potential within 10 meters[/b] to maintain its role as the "king of close-quarters combat." Testing shows that after these changes, shotgun win rates dropped by [b]8%[/b], but their [b]interactive counterplay with other weapons improved significantly.[/b]

The goal is to [b]encourage smarter positioning and timing when using shotguns,[/b] rather than relying solely on range advantage.

[h2]2.3 Weapon Adjustments Based on a "Weapon Ecosystem" Rethink[/h2]

This round of weapon balancing was guided by a data-driven analysis of multiple factors, including kill distance, headshot rate, and other key metrics to ensure all changes are well-supported. Our primary focus was [b]sharpening role differentiation between weapons[/b] to create a more complementary tactical system, while also [b]raising skill ceilings to reward player mastery and prevent extreme power imbalances.[/b] These adjustments aim to promote strategic variety and maintain fair, competitive gameplay.

Moving forward, weapon tuning will remain an ongoing process. These adjustments aren’t just about design philosophy, they’re also influenced by unforeseen issues (e.g., bugs or unintended interactions). [b]Your feedback is critical.[/b] When we spot widespread player reports or abnormal backend data, we’ll act quickly to refine the experience.

For example, yesterday’s patch addressed the M88 silencer attachment’s overpowered state, a design oversight we initially missed. We deeply appreciate players who provided detailed data, enabling us to deploy a swift fix.

[b]Keep sharing your insights![/b] Together, we’ll keep improving Wild Assault’s combat depth.

[h1]3. Valiant Balancing[/h1]

[h2]3.1 Why Does Jack Keep Getting Nerfed?[/h2]

As mentioned earlier, our balancing philosophy follows a data-driven approach, and Jack’s adjustments were made under the same careful consideration. We analyzed both [b]backend statistics and player feedback[/b] to determine the necessary changes.

Jack has always been a highly debated valiant, with opinions sharply divided on his strength. Key points of debate include: the difficulty and power of his sniper rifles, his tactical ability (Q) dealing damage through cover, his signature ability (E) providing wallhack vision, his ultimate ability (Z) being available too frequently, the effectiveness of his SMG loadout, and his stacking power in coordinated squads.

This round of adjustments aims to create a more balanced and enjoyable combat experience while addressing long-standing issues in Jack’s design.

As the first and currently only scout in the game, Jack was forced to fulfill the most traditional role of the class, providing battlefield intelligence for allies in his area. [b]This necessitated a large-scale, long-range reconnaissance tool as his "core skill."[/b] However, this clashed with his animal theming as a wolf: [b]A creature whose senses (like smell) work subtly and continuously, not in sudden bursts.[/b] To reconcile this, we initially gave him a wide-ranging, spammable scouting ability, a decision that, in hindsight, violated basic balancing principles. But since Jack had to be a wolf, we kept the mechanic as an experiment.

Unsurprisingly, this proved once again that cutting corners in design will always backfire when tested by players. This is a lesson we’ve now learned the hard way. Jack’s balance predictably collapsed, forcing us to prioritize healthier gameplay and realign him with his intended scout class. For now, this is a stopgap measure. Like all the Wild Ones, we want Jack to fight as a wolf, but his current "traditional scout" constraints hold him back. When more scouts join the roster, Jack will no longer need to "fill the role" and can finally embrace his true nature — a rebirth we look forward to.

[h2]3.2 Why Will Hongying Get a Smoke Mechanic?[/h2]

As a medic, Hongying is designed to serve the critical role of reviving teammates during intense combat. We recognize that performing revives carries significant risk, so providing reasonable cover felt like a natural solution.

Initially, Hongying’s design included this capability. However, to better emphasize her animal-inspired traits, we shifted focus toward agility and mobile revive gameplay — removing the cover ability and enhancing her mobility and revive mechanics to balance risk and reward.

During testing, we received consistent feedback regarding the medic role’s need for revive cover. After observing actual gameplay, we realized that the risks far outweighed the benefits, as mobility alone couldn’t fully compensate for the lack of cover during revives. This highlighted a need to better balance her role’s functionality with her animal-themed characteristics.

Due to tight development schedules, this adjustment wasn’t finalized in the current version. As mentioned earlier, we’ve added it to our future update plans.

[h1]4. Matchmaking[/h1]

Since the Early Access launch, we've been continuously monitoring match quality, which fluctuates in real-time based on player population. During this period, we've made multiple adjustments to provide the best possible gameplay experience.

Wild Assault has a well-developed matchmaking system, but the final outcome depends on the number of available players at any given time.

Regarding matchmaking, we're aware of the major pain points:
[list]
[*] Low player population leading to uneven matches.
[*] Large skill gaps between teams.
[*] Solo players facing premade squads.
[*] New players matched against veterans.
[*] Back-to-back intense matches feeling exhausting.
[/list]
[b]In our last update, we adjusted matchmaking parameters based on real-time player numbers to better accommodate different skill levels and playtime preferences.[/b] That said, with a limited playerbase, we can't guarantee perfect matches yet, but we're actively exploring optimizations and will keep refining the system based on live data.

Looking ahead, we'll also expand gameplay variety to deliver more diverse experiences for all players.

[h1]5. Netcode[/h1]

Since Wild Assault is a globally launched game, network conditions vary across regions, leading to complex connectivity issues.

We’ve received feedback from players in certain areas, especially regarding high latency and unstable connections, and have prioritized these issues for immediate improvement. Currently, we’re actively collecting and analyzing network data to implement optimizations as soon as possible.

Thank you for your patience! We’ll keep you updated on our progress.

[h1]6. Current Development Progress[/h1]

Now that Wild Assault has entered a weekly update phase, many of you have expressed curiosity about our current development focus. Firstly, addressing critical issues remains our top priority. We are constantly working to reproduce, identify, and resolve problems based on your detailed feedback (thank you again!) At the same time, we’re also dedicating significant effort to new content development. Here are some exciting details we’d like to share:
[list]
[*] [b]New Game Mode: [/b]A new game mode is coming in Season 1! Once the core functionality is ready, we plan to conduct small scale test runs. Stay tuned for updates!
[*] [b]Season 2 New Map Update: [/b]Whitebox testing is finished, and we’re moving into detailed map design this week! We're refining the layout with more detailed designs for pathways, structures, and obstacles.
[*] [b]New Valiant: [/b]Meet Crock... Soon! We’ve completed the modeling, 3C refinement, SFX design, and animations for this new Valiant. We hope you’ll love this fierce, relentless, and cold-blooded warrior when they arrive in Season 2!
[*] [b]Achievement: [/b]As of May 8th, we’ve received 552 submissions for the Achievement System Design Survey. Your creativity sparked some bold new directions for our team! Many of these ideas are now being reimagined and brought to life by our artists. Thank you for the inspiration!
[/list]

BTW, we’re planning to introduce a new female valiant in a future update! What animal would you like her to be? Share your ideas with us!
Survey: https://wjx.cn/vm/PmpuMaZ.aspx

notes.title: Wild Assault Early Access: Producer's Note April 17
notes.content:
Hello Wild Ones,

I am Lantin, head of Combat Cat Studio and the producer behind Wild Assault. What a week it has been since we launched into Early Access on April 11! On behalf of the entire team, I want to thank you for your support and for all the invaluable bug reports and suggestions. This feedback is precisely why we are committed to making the most of Early Access to elevate Wild Assault to the next level. Now, allow me to address some of your most pressing questions and dive into what is coming next.

It has been an exciting week, for us obviously, and for you as well we hope. The team evaluates community feedback, social media comments, and ingame feedback on a daily basis. We have been working at full power on bug fixes and gameplay improvements.

As of today, we have issued hotfixes daily (including weekends). 6 hotfixes have been deployed, addressing more than 50 bugs and improving the overall gameplay experience across multiple aspects.
We identified and resolved the matchmaking issue that led to a noticeable shortage of actual players in some rounds.
[list]
[*] We added the Invert Mouse Y Axis settings option to better serve your gaming needs.
[*] We have removed the Battle Pass weekly XP cap (which previously limited player progress) after reviewing community feedback. Compensation has also been issued.
[*] We have also made further adjustments to the matchmaking system based on current player counts and server status. This remains an ongoing task requiring constant evaluation and fine-tuning.
[*] We have increased the Valiant proficiency earned from matches, as requested by the community.
[/list]
[b]For the full list of changes, please refer to the previous patch notes.[/b]

With your support and the developers hard work, the current build is now much more stable, ensuring a solid gameplay experience. Over the next week, we will continue addressing known issues and implementing improvements focused on critical aspects. After that, we will dedicate more development time to the new content we have prepared for this season. Our overall strategy is as follows:
[list]
[*] Critical issues will always be prioritized and resolved as quickly as possible. This remains our top commitment.
[*] We have also prepared exciting and interesting events for this season, and we will share more details soon.
[*] As planned, each season will last for 3 months. During each season, we aim to introduce different game modes, new maps, and new Valiants.
[/list]
[b]We also plan to release an updated roadmap for Wild Assault. Please follow our social media channels to stay informed.[/b]

We understand that trust is not built easily, especially across national borders, time zones, cultural differences, and diverse ways of life. However, the studio and I firmly believe that through transparency, consistent communication, and a shared passion for this project, we can bridge these gaps and forge a strong, lasting connection.

We are amazed by the fan art you have created, touched by your reviews on Steam, inspired by the creative suggestions you have shared, and motivated by the passion you have expressed for Wild Assault. All of this has reinforced our belief in you, in ourselves, and in the potential we are building together.

Thank you again. Hope to talk to you soon in the next episode. Good hunting!


Lantin
Producer | Combat Cat Studio

notes.title: Wild Assault Early Access FAQ
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/c8c818c7fae01bbb9d6c768dedccb72b05c9bc63.png[/img]

Hello Wild Ones!

The long-awaited April 11th is finally here! We sincerely welcome you to join the Wild Assault Early Access ride!

Staying true to our commitment of co-creating with our players, Wild Assault has undergone four rounds of public testing since its initial reveal on January 18th, 2024. During this time, we’ve collected and analyzed tens of thousands of pieces of player feedback, carefully listening to your suggestions and enthusiasm. Through our dev logs, we’ve maintained close interaction and collaboration with you all. Your input has significantly shaped the game in many aspects.

We’re pleased to see that this game development model has been well-received. Since the conclusion of Wild Assault Weekly, we’ve often been asked: “When will you release the next episode?” We’re also exploring better ways to communicate with our players. The Early Access version marks a new beginning for Wild Assault. To express our gratitude for your continuous support, we’ll continue to maintain a steady update schedule and remain open in our communication with you.

We’d like to take this opportunity to share our upcoming update plans and address some of the questions that have been on your minds.

[h1]1. What's Next[/h1]

[h2]1.1 Update Plans[/h2]

[h3]1.1.1 Hotfixes[/h3]

After releasing the Early Access version, we will address feedback through small hotfixes. While these updates will be smaller in scale compared to previous ones, they will allow us to quickly fix bugs and improve content based on community feedback, thereby positively impacting the game’s overall polish. While prioritizing critical issues that affect the gameplay experience, we will also gradually meet your diverse needs.

[h3]1.1.2 Feedback Channels[/h3]

If you encounter bugs, hacking, or other issues that severely impact your gaming experience, you can submit feedback through the in-game feedback portal. We will promptly identify and resolve these issues. Thank you for your active feedback and support for the game.

We also plan to release dev logs on a regular basis to address the key concerns raised by the community. To ensure the steady advancement of Wild Assault’s development, we need to thoroughly discuss and validate all types of feedback before jumping to conclusions. This is why we believe dev logs are still the best way to communicate with you about the things you care about. We appreciate your patience and understanding, as this more deliberate communication approach will lead to more effective problem-solving.

[h1]Wild Assault Early Access FAQ[/h1]

[h2]2.1 Can you introduce the pricing?[/h2]

We are offering two versions: the Standard Edition and the Supporter Edition. The Standard Edition is priced at $15 (regional pricing may apply). Additionally, we have introduced a Supporter Edition this time, which includes a discounted bundle for the Supporter DLC (of course, if you purchase the base game first, you can still buy the DLC later at the discounted bundle price).

[h2]2.2 What’s in the Battle Pass?[/h2]

[b]The basic Battle Pass is free for players with access to Wild Assault Early Access. It includes the new Valiant character Erwin, multiple new weapons, and cosmetic items.
The premium Battle Pass can be unlocked by spending a certain amount of Beast Coins. It includes the "Erwin - Field Medic Commander" cosmetics, new weapon cosmetics, and a Beast Coins reward.[/b]

[h2]2.3 Will you paywall the Valiants or weapons in the future?[/h2]

[b]No. We guarantee you that all Valiants and weapons will be unlockable through free methods.[/b]

[h2]2.4 Will there be a creator program?[/h2]

We're working on it. We will definitely keep you posted on our periodic creator program events.

[h1]3. Technical Troubleshooting[/h1]

[h2]3.1 Download & Install[/h2]

[h3]Q: How do I download Wild Assault? Can I still use the client from the previous test?[/h3]

A: The Wild Assault Early Access introduces a new game client, which is purchasable on Steam. Please uninstall all previously installed Wild Assault game clients (playtest or demo) to avoid unexpected game launch issues.

[h3]Q: What should I do if the installation fails?[/h3]

A: Please make sure your device has enough storage space. At least 20GB of free space is required for the demo build.

[h2]3.2 Tech Issues[/h2]

[h3]Q: Do I need latency booster apps for this test?[/h3]

A: The early access battle servers are located in Asia (Singapore), the United States (Northern Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt), and South America (São Paulo). Feel free to try some of the ping boosters based on your location.

[h3]Q: I encountered a DirectX 12 error when launching the game. How can I resolve it?[/h3]

A: If you’re experiencing a DirectX 12 error when launching the game, we recommend checking the following:
[olist]
[*] Update your graphics driver. Visit the official website of your graphics card manufacturer to download the latest driver, or use the Nvidia App to update automatically. Ensure your graphics driver is up to date.
[*] Update your Windows OS. Make sure your Windows 10 64-bit OS is updated to version 1909 or later. This update is crucial for DirectX 12 support. We recommend updating to version 21H1 or later.
[*] Check the minimum graphics card requirements. Verify if your graphics card meets the minimum requirements: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060, AMD Radeon RX 560, or Intel ARC A380.
[*] If you have other issues, feel free to join our official Discord for assistance: https://discord.gg/WildAssault
[/olist]

[h3]Q: What should I do if the game fails to launch or if I encounter other issues?[/h3]

A: If your system meets the requirements, please try updating your graphics drivers, clearing memory or freeing up disk space. If the game still won’t launch, right-click on the game in your Steam library, go to Properties, and verify the integrity of the game files. For other solutions, please check the Tech Troubleshooting in our official Discord server: discord.gg/wildassault


[h3]Q: What should I do if I encounter low frame rates or stuttering?[/h3]

A1: 
[list]
[*] If you're experiencing low frame rates, open the operating system's Task Manager to check the CPU and GPU usage.
[*] If the GPU usage is consistently high, nearing 100%, try lowering the graphics settings to improve the game's frame rate. For example, switch to medium or lower quality, reduce the game resolution, and lower the rendering quality to avoid low frame rates due to insufficient GPU performance.
[*] If the CPU usage is high, you can improve the frame rate by lowering vegetation density, shadow quality, visual distance, and disabling vertical sync.
[*] Additionally, you can limit the frame rate cap to a stable 30 or 60 FPS for a smoother gaming experience.
[/list]
A2: Try the following solutions
[list]
[*] It’s recommended to install the game on a SSD to significantly enhance gameplay smoothness.
[*] Ensure that your computer has at least 20GB of free memory available to avoid high memory usage that may cause stuttering.
[*] Set the power plan in the Control Panel to "High Performance." For laptops, it's advised to run the game while plugged in, ensuring proper device cooling.
[*] Close unnecessary background programs and services to free up more system resources for the game.
[*] Update your graphics drivers to ensure they are the latest, which can improve game performance and avoid compatibility issues.
[/list]

[h2]3.3 System Requirements[/h2]

[h3]MINIMUM[/h3]
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10 (64-bit) or later
[*] CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 1600 或 Core i5 6600K
[*] RAM: 8 GB RAM
[*] GPU: Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060 or AMD Radeon RX 580 or Intel ARC A380
[*] DirectX Version: 12
[*] Storage: 20 GB
[/list]
[h3]RECOMMENDED[/h3]
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10 (64-bit) or later
[*] CPU:  AMD Ryzen 7 2700X or Intel Core i7 4790
[*] RAM: 16 GB RAM
[*] GPU: Nvidia GeForce RTX 3060 or AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT or Intel ARC A750
[*] DirectX Version: 12
[*] Storage: 20 GB, SSD required
[/list]

notes.title: Wild Assault Early Access Q&A
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/093a2a2a80199fdb302bccfddc48270b268040a7.png[/img]

Thank you for your attention and support, Wild Ones! Recently, our community has been discussing Wild Assault’s Early Access release. Combat Cat Studio would like to share the reasoning and vision behind this decision.

[h2]"What is Steam Early Access?"[/h2]

[quote=Steam Support] Early Access is a unique development model that allows games to be played as they progress towards a full release. Early Access encourages ongoing updates from developers, while letting players participate in direct feedback through gameplay and community involvement. [/quote]
More here: https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/6554-ED29-FBDB-1612


[h2]"Why release the game as Steam Early Access?"[/h2]

Combat Cat Studio is a team of over 20 friends who share the same vision and passion for shooter games. We aimed to create a unique game that could bring joy to the community and ourselves. That's how Wild Assault came to life. From April 2024 to Early Access, we've conducted four open tests. During this journey, we were fortunate enough to receive countless help, feedback, support, and recognition from our community, which allowed us to further polish this project in the right direction. Now that we have enough content for players to fully and sustainably experience Wild Assault, we’ve decided to enter the Early Access phase. We hope to continue collecting valuable feedback from our players during this stage and work tirelessly to reach the next phase: the final release.

[h2]"How long will Wild Assault be in Early Access?"[/h2]

Combat Cat Studio plans to continue enriching the content and polishing the gameplay experience of the Early Access version for one year until it reaches the final release stage.

[h2]"How different will the final release be compared to the Early Access version?"[/h2]

In addition to addressing basic issues and optimizing the experience for the Early Access version, we aim to continue creating new content based on our roadmap for at least one year. [b]We also plan to further explore possibilities with the Steam Workshop, improved social features, Valiant interaction experiences, Valiant customization, and much more, all to deliver engaging gameplay for our players.[/b]

[h2]"What is the current state of the Early Access version?"[/h2]

The Wild Assault Early Access version offers [b]10 Valiants, 30 weapons, 2 game modes, 3 maps, and dozens of cosmetic appearances.[/b] It also features a comprehensive tutorial, a Valiant proficiency system, a gunsmith system, and game seasons. Compared to the open test version, we’ve further improved game performance, UI/UX, and visual quality based on community feedback. We hope you enjoy what we have to offer in Early Access!

[h2]"Will you adjust the game price once it reaches the final release stage?"[/h2]

[b]We believe the current price (TBA) reflects the unfinished state of the Early Access version and is a way to express our gratitude to players who actively support the game during this stage. We also promise that all basic Valiants and weapons will be permanently available through free unlockable methods. [/b] We plan to slightly adjust the final release price based on the new content and features added during the Early Access phase. However, rest assured, we will ensure the pricing remains fair and reasonable based on the game’s content quality and our community’s feedback.

[h2]"How is the community involved during the game's development, according to your plan?"[/h2]

Combat Cat Studio has been actively following community discussions and collecting feedback on the Steam community and other social media platforms. Additionally, we’ve implemented an in-game feedback function to make it easier for players to express their ideas with us. Moving forward, we will continue to stay connected with our community through developer logs, keeping everyone updated on what we’ve been working on. Lastly, we warmly invite all players interested in Wild Assault to join our community and share your thoughts with us!


Hope that answers some of your questions!

Calling all Wild Ones!

It’s been a while! Combat Cat Studio has received over 2,000 suggestions and feedback of all kinds since the gamma test in October 2024, guiding us through the last stretch of darkness before the dawn breaks. This time, we’re excited to show you how much Wild Assault has evolved over the past 100+ days and nights.
[list]
[*] Over 600 bugs have been fixed.
[*] Performance Optimization: Frame rates have been significantly boosted across LOW, MID, and HIGH graphics presets. Visual quality has also been improved under LOW and MID graphics presets.
[*] New Content and Systems: Check out the details below!

[list]
[*] Bug Reports: This time we’re using GitHub to track bugs for better bug report management and workflow! For more details, please visit our bug tracker page on GitHub: https://github.com/CombatCatCommunity/BugTracker

notes.title: Wild Assault Dev Log: 2024 Recap
notes.content:
Hello Wild Ones! 🎩👌

How time flies! We posted the first Wild Assault Dev Log on June 13, 2024, and now all of a sudden, you're reading the 22nd log we've posted. ✍️

According to our plan, [b]this will be the last dev log you read before Wild Assault enters early access.[/b] So let's take some time to highlight some of the most memorable moments from the past year! 📸

After years of development, Wild Assault first went public on [b]January 18, 2024[/b]. It’s been an amazing year for us, and we’re so glad that you’ve embraced our little project and walked with us along the way.

[h1]Alpha Test[/h1]

Wild Assault's Alpha Test began in [b]early May 2024[/b], and we clearly didn’t expect that much attention. 

Our Steam page received over 300k views in the first five days of the alpha test, and more than 40k players from all over the world applied to participate. Gameplay videos posted by players on multiple social media platforms generated over 3 million views.

We were caught off guard at first but managed to quickly build a functioning community and feedback mechanism. Thanks to your attention and continuous support, we were invited to the Anthro Festival 2024 on Steam. Thank you [b]Klace[/b]! What an honor!

Special thanks to [b]Auxl, Bliz, Frizzey, Hilda, Tonky, VoiL and Yonu[/b] for being the best Discord mods ever! ❤️
Again, a big thanks to [b]DoryuuZ[/b]. You are one of the best content creators we’ve worked with! 🫡

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/bcbd178901bac01c4c89c181a4fae5c3ddbb374b.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/1930c5a1a00abfb2abe7ebe076acb873bec7beca.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/e806c7b404871d2dbad593ef1708a0736a6e418a.png[/img]
[h1]Beta Test[/h1]

Wild Assault Beta Test: Assemble went live on [b]August 1, 2024[/b], alongside our first official trailer. What started as a "side project" was once again warmly received by our community and players. The trailer generated over 1.1 million views across all social media platforms, and we received countless positive comments and feedback.

[previewyoutube=iXSrWOjuZLk;full][/previewyoutube]
During the beta test, more than 300 gameplay and review clips were uploaded to video platforms like YouTube, gathering 1.5 million views. Wild Assault also caught the attention of streamers, many of whom began streaming it on Twitch. The beta test achieved over 90k watch hours and peaked with more than 50k viewers throughout the beta test.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/a558b7a807e0b7638e08969143fe6a5fc724a068.png[/img]
[h1]Tokyo Game Show 2024[/h1]

In [b]late September 2024[/b], we traveled to Tokyo, Japan, to attend the Tokyo Game Show 2024, one of the biggest events we’ve ever participated in. By setting up a booth on-site, we showcased Wild Assault’s core gameplay and eye-catching features to hundreds of attendees during the event. Our producer Lantin also presented Wild Assault to an even larger audience through the TGS official live show. By attending TGS 2024, we were able to go beyond borders, make new friends, and introduce our project to their communities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/ff5d3677f88abb4b077b3d6d8049b2ec7504957d.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/780d63b502fc0373c867aff4b24bf1e2eca9535a.png[/img]
[h1]Gamma Test & Steam Next Fest[/h1]

Our third open test, the Wild Assault Gamma Test, began on [b]October 9, 2024[/b], during the Steam Next Fest 2024. Our team successfully pushed updates daily, addressing over 700 issues submitted by our community throughout the test. By our estimation, posts with the hashtag #WildAssault received over 1.1 million views across social media platforms. We saw many amazing streams, clips, and fan art created during the gamma test. We are truly amazed by your creativity and sincerely thankful for the support from our wonderful community！

[previewyoutube=Pjf-dWWxT7w;full][/previewyoutube]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/72eba10072e1ade56beab392058dd32ce80d2533.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/c3f29773d4e77994ed97e33aa0507b2ae4ba052d.png[/img] Art by [url=https://x.com/teteteko/status/1845444346709147929]@teteteko[/url]

In collaboration with [b]CShip, HOWL, Klace, Maxi Molina, and Studio Klondike[/b], we attended the SXSW Game Show in Sydney, Australia, expanding Wild Assault to even more continents. You guys are some of the most amazing indie game devs we’ve ever had the pleasure of working with! Thank you so much for your help, we owe you one!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/f26ab9b43baddbe632a7435b8f3559e233ac08fc.jpg[/img]
Through your invaluable support and our collective efforts, Wild Assault made it to the "Most Wishlisted Upcoming Games" chart in the Steam Next Fest October 2024 Edition, an achievement we never dreamed possible!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/71dbe79cc8128bd056c2f935f99e7781f7425ef2.png[/img]
[h1]The Next Step[/h1]

Our community is the most precious treasure we have. Wild Assault now enjoys more than 100k followers and community members across various social media platforms, bringing together [b]players, esports elites, indie game devs, streamers, YouTubers, VTubers, artists, cosplayers, and voice actors[/b]. Wild Assault has become a project co-created by each and every one of us. Through tests, feedback, suggestions and fan art, our community has made Wild Assault more alive and creative than ever. We are proud to be part of this journey, and you should be too!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/7d0c55847fb4a04654bba94209a12e569d20d481.png[/img]
To continue co-creating Wild Assault with our community, we have been posting this dev log on a weekly basis. Our dev logs have generated over 1 million impressions across Steam and social media platforms, gathering enormous comments, likes and feedback. We’ve truly enjoyed sharing our development process with you all and have confidently relied on your input to guide our decisions. We couldn’t have done it without your love and support!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/3b68b6eb53beac8be975b860d5530b85b884eca3.png[/img]

Since the gamma test, we’ve been working hard to prepare new content for early access, hoping that [b]features like new valiants, maps, systems, grind content, trailers, and key art[/b] meet your expectations. On the tech side, we've focused on improving game performance and server stability, resolving over 100 issues based on your previous feedback. If you've been following our previous dev logs, you probably have a good sense of what we’ve been working on lately. [b]We’re also preparing to reveal more info about the new content before early access — they’re really cool and you’ll definitely like them![/b]

📣 By the way, [b]we’re happy to let you know that there will be another QoS focused open test before we enter early access[/b]! Please consider adding Wild Assault to your Steam wishlist so you’ll be notified once our test is ready.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2827230/Wild_Assault/

Thank you so much! Wild Assault early access is on the horizon. Let's make it happen!

notes.title: Wild Assault Dev Log: Dive into Performance Optimizations - A Case Study
notes.content:
Hello, Wild Ones! We're excited to talk to you again in this episode!

First of all, we’re thrilled to see that so many players love our early concept designs for Akai Hime. The team is already discussing the possibility of making them cosmetics for Akai Hime in the future. We’ll definitely keep you updated on our progress!

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/b86af4ef1b1def9cafefdffb8cade9724e34dfcb.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/4ea9e2e28baed0856130909cbc157505efc82c3e.png[/img][/url]
Emote by [url=https://x.com/Glitterissafe]Glitter[/url]

In this episode, we’d like to share a case study on how we continue to optimize Wild Assault’s graphics performance.

[h1]Handy Tools in the Gearbox[/h1]

Combat Cat Studio is a small group of developers. To improve overall development efficiency for such a huge and complex project, we decided to utilize some of the most innovative tools available in the latest version of Unreal Engine 5, including [b]Nanite, Lumen, and VSM,[/b] to achieve stunning visual effects like [b]Dynamic Global Illumination[/b].

[quote] [h3]Technical Terms[/h3]

💡 [b]Nanite[/b]: [i]A powerful system for rendering ultra-detailed geometry, enabling rich, immersive experiences without sacrificing performance.[/i]
💡 [b]Lumen[/b]: [i]A real-time global illumination and reflections system, delivering natural and dynamic lighting for immersive environments.[/i]
💡 [b]VSM[/b]: [i]A high-performance shadow-mapping system that delivers soft, stable, and detailed shadows for realistic visuals.[/i]

📖 [b]Explore More from the Epic Games Dev Community:[/b]

1️⃣ [i][url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/nanite-virtualized-geometry-in-unreal-engine]Nanite Virtualized Geometry[/url][/i]
2️⃣ [i][url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/lumen-global-illumination-and-reflections-in-unreal-engine]Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections[/url][/i]
3️⃣ [i][url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/virtual-shadow-maps-in-unreal-engine]Virtual Shadow Maps in Unreal Engine[/url][/i]
4️⃣ [i][url=https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/tutorials/PWdG/dynamic-global-illumination-methods]Dynamic Global Illumination Methods[/url][/i]
[/quote]
However, the new technologies offered in Unreal Engine 5 are relatively [b]hardware intensive[/b] and could introduce performance issues in the game. We've been conducting all kinds of experiments to address these performance issues ever since the alpha test. Specifically, one of the most important questions we're trying to answer is: "[b]How can we further optimize the loading and rendering process in a large, open world created using UE5?[/b]"

After months of exploration, we are finally making progress. We've tested the latest build of Wild Assault with the [b]HIGH graphics preset on an RTX 3070 Ti GPU[/b], and [b]the average FPS has increased by 7.2%[/b] compared to a prior build without the new methods implemented.

[h1]"Let'em Cook!"[/h1]

[h2]"NOT a Piece of Cake"[/h2]

Unreal Engine 5 offers a variety of efficiency driven tools that make it easier for developers to achieve their goals. Initially, we considered using the [b]World Partition[/b] feature to[b] automatically divide the open world into several grids, loading them only when needed[/b]. Additionally, we planned to utilize the [b]HLOD (Hierarchical Level of Detail) system[/b] to [b]render models at varying levels of detail[/b].

By combining these two features, we could load only the necessary grids of the open world, render objects near the camera at a high level of detail, and display objects farther away with lower levels of detail. This approach can significantly reduce hardware demand (including GPU workload and VRAM usage) while ensuring a high and stable frame rate.

Problem solved, right? Or is it?

[quote][h3]Demonstration[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/25894fd0fc74f6e148544dbdadd69c5d285167cb.png[/img]
[b]Wild Assault Operation Mojave World Partition Demonstration[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/02ccdd7b8b35343757bad75c39b87557710c522f.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/7a09ee1fb961c6e3b456a8639b157ace3bd8f3ca.png[/img]
[b]Wild Assault Operation Mojave HLOD Demonstration
The tower is rendered in high detail when the camera is near but in low detail when the camera is far.[/b][/quote]
[quote] [h3]Technical Terms[/h3]

💡 [b]World Partition[/b]: [i]A system that splits large game worlds into smaller grids and loads only what's needed, improving performance.[/i]
💡 [b]HLOD[/b]: [i]A feature that shows nearby objects in high detail and distant ones in lower detail to optimize rendering.[/i]

📖 [b]Explore More from the Epic Games Dev Community:[/b]

1️⃣ [i][url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/world-partition-in-unreal-engine]World Partition in Unreal Engine[/url][/i]
2️⃣ [i][url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/hierarchical-level-of-detail-in-unreal-engine]Hierarchical Level of Detail in Unreal Engine[/url][/i]
[/quote]
Test runs reveal that the problem is more complicated than it initially seemed. World Partition's dynamic grid loading often causes [b]significant frame rate stutter[/b], an issue that’s unacceptable for a competitive, fast paced PVP shooter like Wild Assault.

What if we make the grids bigger? That could prevent the HLOD system from working effectively. It seems we’ll need to further develop a customized approach to implementing HLOD. 🤔

[h2]"We're Goin' Custom Shop!"[/h2]

By default, Unreal Engine manages the HLOD system automatically. To better control how the engine renders different levels of detail, we modified its source code to make the system more customizable. We also added various configuration parameters to fine-tune the process.

[b](Fellow indie devs, feel free to DM us if you want to learn the trick!) [/b]

[h3]Solving HLOD Visual Defects[/h3]

Some objects displayed noticeable visual defects after merging, indicating the need for rules to better manage how HLOD is applied to specific objects. [b]We have further developed a set of rules for all relevant objects and applied HLOD accordingly.[/b] In addition, [b]we have also modified the implementation of the HLOD layer[/b] to achieve a balance between visual quality and frame rate performance.

[quote][h3]Demonstration[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/13aceff06fa0088575696604b7fa920304ef9548.png[/img]

[b]Wild Assault Custom HLOD Demonstration
Original model, model with visual defects caused by auto HLOD, and model processed with custom HLOD.[/b]
[/quote]
[h3]Solving Performance Drops in Multiplayer Mode[/h3]

Wait that's not the end of it!

While our custom HLOD solution has significantly improved frame rate performance in singleplayer mode, it didn’t work as expected in multiplayer mode, even after we removed all dynamic components.
After a careful investigation, we discovered that [b]the loading order of different levels of detail (LODs)[/b], along with [b]a related VFX frequently applied to textures like terrain, roads, and vegetation[/b], was negatively impacting frame rate performance.

We then developed specific solutions to address the issues we identified.

As a result of our custom HLOD R&D, we boosted FPS in our test build by approximately 7.2%. We hope this example provides [b]a simple and transparent look at our performance optimization workflow[/b]. As our producer mentioned in the previous Q&A sessions, performance optimization is always an ongoing task for us. We’ll continue exploring new methods to improve Wild Assault's frame rate and deliver the best possible gaming experience.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/3e818acc5192c529679d89050947eacf4b619927.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/1310004566a27dd1630a24cbf81a1486fd818321.png[/img][/url]
Emote by [url=https://x.com/Glitterissafe]Glitter[/url]

We hope you enjoyed this week’s geeky dev log, and we truly appreciate your support! We’ll keep striving to find better ways to discuss tech topics with both players and fellow indie devs. Let us know your thoughts!



Don't forget to add Wild Assault to your wishlist! 🫶

notes.title: Wild Assault Dev Log: Shreds of Lore
notes.content:
Hello Wild Ones! It's me Vincent again!

[b]First of all, Combat Cat Studio would like to wish you a Merry Christmas![/b] We hope you truly enjoy this holiday time with your family, friends, and loved ones.
The holidays are a great time for stories! In this episode, let me be the storyteller and reveal what had happened in the Wild Assault universe for you.

[h1]One[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/901995ce6266f13801dec14cb2d221e66fdad519.jpg[/img]Art by [url=https://discord.com/channels/1209429896317771796/1236495404296573038/1236495404296573038]15218[/url]

Times Square is always crowded.

The clock tower's hands slowly turn back to a time when the economy was still promising. A street performer plays his guitar while the corner record store blasts "Thriller."

That figure finally appeared — when I first met Norman, I was a profiler at the Serene Confidential Intl. Org. and hadn't yet turned 30. Norman, on the other hand, was a young soldier in the army — and one of my subjects.

Back then, the young yet experienced private was full of ambition, with no failed assessments in his record. His left eye still saw the world just as you and I do.

Pvt. Norman, a.k.a. Subject Norman, had a close relationship with reconnaissance personnel named Jack. Regarding Jack, I remember writing the following in my report at the time: Lonesome and sensitive. Intentionally avoids social contact. It was quite troublesome to approach him, even if I was observing from a mile away. It felt as if he could sense all living souls that are aware of his presence... There's still a .338 bullet lodged in my left shoulder that doctors haven't been able to remove.

It took my colleagues and me great pains to finally extract a few photos of them from the developing solution. These were among the few materials we gathered on these subjects for the organization. Now, ten years later, those files have already been classified and sealed as top secrets by Serene.

[h1]Two[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/43c4d9a964b045ef2ec77451adf0524276ad28fe.png[/img]
"Nah, I'd win" by [url=https://discord.com/channels/1209429896317771796/1271906737657479189/1271906737657479189]BlackBliz[/url]

At the WealthGuard BioTech Research Institute, I met Lianhua (Lotus), Hongying's mother, a nice and calm lady. While we talked in her lab, the one standing next to Lianhua was Marquez, a new graduate obsessed with studies about "biological life forms" and "immortality."

Marquez was having a rough time with her research back then. She often locked herself up in the lab, day and night, putting her health aside. As Marquez's mentor, Lianhua suggested that she dial it down a little and truly experience life besides studying it. 

The deep green liquid in the swaying test tube Marquez held glimmered faintly. Perhaps it was destined that Marquez would walk a path totally separate from her mentor's.

[h1]Three[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/b55d643284cfc84cecfb40f0599a68293ca2dfea.jpg[/img]
Art By [url=https://x.com/teteteko/status/1845444346709147929]@Teteteko[/url]

Hongying.

I learned that name many years later, on the day she pointed a gun at my head. I guessed she had always been a good child.

That year, when I was about to be executed for rebellion. On the other side of the barbed wire, she reached out her hand and gave me a candy.

Was it candy? By then, I had already lost my sense of taste because of the drugs they forced me to swallow during the tortures.

What was it I held in my hand? My intuition was the only thing I could rely on to make a guess.

[h1]Four[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/19cda928ea61264774f43dc848e429e618eb50bb.jpg[/img]Art by [url=https://x.com/NemeaNReiN/status/1803472630315622819]@NemeaNReiN[/url]

The war concluded, and I was pardoned for the rebellion, with my shackles removed.

Our ship once again docked at the very same place. Gunshots echoed through the neighborhood, and all I could see were herds fleeing the chaos. Amidst the conflict stood a huge chunk of beef — the infamous Ryan, who could navigate both the bureaus and the skid rows unscathed.

[h1]Five[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/2f024ec3c4f797370a7945884c2858bb45d93fcb.jpg[/img]Art by [url=https://x.com/NemeaNReiN/status/1800571161937613132]@NemeaNReiN[/url]

The European journey was quite hurried, leaving me only enough time to sketch a brief outline.

We crossed countless mountains later on to reach a quiet town beside the snowy plains. I saw fear in the eyes of the residents — the cruel and greedy mayor had governed them for ages, stripping away the last bit of vitality from this poor town.

On a night without a shred of starlight or moonlight, the mayor fell from the town tower and paid his debt. There appeared Vladimir, the herd's most friendly neighbor.

The wind scattered sparks into the dark night sky, spreading like stars.

[h1]Six[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899972/7deecdf9f5c0eae0ee308e553f739ed2429ba51d.jpg[/img]Art by [url=https://www.artstation.com/artwork/3EoGZE]Louis Wood[/url]

The road turns south, and things go south — the inevitable. 

Rain night, neon lights, chatter and laughter, beers and wine. One of our assets stepped into Akai Hime's carefully crafted trap. What are the odds? It seemed Akai Hime did not intend to wrap it up there. 

Later on, the asset informed me that Akai Hime finally agreed to "their" terms, leaving the realm she built bare-handed and entering another territory.

[h1]Seven[/h1]

We crossed the long coast and reached the other side at last. Passing by me, alongside the sea breeze, was Uly. 

Uly, who was unemployed for the fourth time, asked me: "Why do you look a bit familiar, mister? Where are you headed? Could I be company?"

[h1]Eight[/h1]

Finally returning to Serene HQ after years of traveling, I logged all my reports for safekeeping. Hopefully, in the future, you, who might be destined to cross paths with my subjects, will have a glimpse of these materials. 

By the time that happens, there may be another war on the horizon. 

...Sorry, could you help push my wheelchair?

——
Side Note: We have been consistently creating and improving the Wild Assault universe, and while there may be contradictions and loopholes in the early designs, we have addressed numerous issues regarding the lore. Please refer to our upcoming latest build as the standard.
Additionally, although the Wild Assault universe contains references or inspirations from reality, it is constructed as an entirely distinct parallel universe. We hope you can be flexible with the details and let us know how we can make it better!
